belief: I must have done something to deserve this.
origins: The mind seeks explanations for pain, and self-blame can feel easier than randomness. Rumination about past mistakes fuels shame.
teaches: Jesus said of those killed in a tragedy, that they were not worse sinners than others (Luke 13:1–5). He said of the blind man, “Neither this man nor his parents sinned.” “The soul who sins is the one who will die,” yet “A son will not bear the iniquity of his father.” Suffering in a fallen world often comes without a proportionate cause. Believers may repent of sin and be forgiven, but suffering is not a ledger of what we deserve.
self_statements: If I had been better, this would not have happened.
errors: Believing suffering is either deserved or random.
Feeling guilty and concluding that I deserve it.
questions: What specifically do I think I did?
Would I say a friend deserved the same illness?
What did Jesus say about suffering and sin?
What has been forgiven and what do I carry?
What caused my illness according to my doctors?
How can I put down self-blame?
truth: My suffering is not a measure of what I deserve. Jesus rejects the simple equation between suffering and sin. I can bring real sin to God for forgiveness and let go of self-blame.
log: Each week, note one thought of self-blame you replaced.
actions: State what you blame yourself for.
Speak to yourself as to a friend.
prayer: Lord, I search my past for a reason. Free me from false guilt, forgive what is real, and comfort me in my suffering. Amen.
